record.paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one find a Poisson bracket P on an affine manifold and a nontrivial Kontsevich graph cocycle action whose induced infinitesimal deformation changes P in a way that is not merely a coordinate change along a vector field, thereby producing a family of inequivalent Poisson structures?

evidence.quote: It remains an open problem to find an example of nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, thus spreading it to a family of inequivalent structures not related by a coordinate change.
Beyond the tetrahedron γ3, there are countably many ‘good’ nontrivial graph cocycles: γ5, γ7, . . .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be an affine manifold and let $P$ be a Poisson bivector on $M$, i.e. a smooth bivector field $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM)$ satisfying $[P,P]=0$ in the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Recall that to every cocycle $\gamma$ in M. Kontsevich's graph complex of finite oriented graphs (with vertices of valency $\geq 3$ and a wedge ordering on edges) one associates, via the orientation morphism, a bivector flow $\dot P=\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)$ that is automatically tangent to the variety of Poisson structures, so that $P_t=P+t\,\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)+O(t^2)$ is an infinitesimal deformation of $P$ through Poisson bivectors. The flow is called trivial at $P$ if there exists a vector field $X$ on $M$ such that $\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)=[P,X]$ (i.e. the deformation is generated by a coordinate change), and nontrivial otherwise. The known nontrivial graph cocycles include the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ and an infinite family $\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots$ of "good" wheel-type cocycles.

Problem. Exhibit an affine manifold $M$, a Poisson bivector $P$ on $M$, and a graph cocycle $\gamma\in\{\gamma_3,\gamma_5,\gamma_7,\dots\}$ such that the induced flow $\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)$ is not of the form $[P,X]$ for any vector field $X$ on $M$, thereby producing a one-parameter family of Poisson structures on $M$ that are pairwise inequivalent under diffeomorphisms of $M$.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Poisson deformations
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) on the action of Kontsevich graph cocycles on Nambu–Poisson brackets show that for the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ on Nambu brackets in low dimensions ($2\le d\le 4$) the induced flow is a Poisson coboundary, i.e. realized by a vector field. No published example of a Poisson bracket on an affine manifold for which a graph cocycle (tetrahedron or higher wheel) produces a deformation that is not a coordinate-change coboundary appears to exist; the problem is explicitly stated as open in the cited series.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, II. The tetrahedral flow is a coboundary in 4D
status_evidence.snippet: For Nambu brackets in dimension up to 4, the tetrahedral graph flow is shown to be a Poisson coboundary.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial results show triviality (coboundary) of the tetrahedron action on Nambu brackets in low dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems regarding nontrivial action of graph cocycles on Poisson brackets.
status_evidence.claim: Problem has been open for several years.
